cat_scale: 12 initially infected cats with long follow-up
design_summary: rechallenge after 39 days and again after 77 months
key_finding: short-term protection against re-shedding was strong, but 4/9 shed again after 77 months
early intestinal stages were suppressed in immune cats
shows T-263 was once advanced toward product development

cat_scale: deterministic simulation seeded with 10 to 50 cats and 0 to 75% vaccination coverage
design_summary: dynamic swine-cat farm model compared field and weaning vaccination schedules while varying cat numbers prevalence and oocyst survival
key_finding: decreased finishing-pig prevalence was driven mainly by fewer cats (sr2=47%) and shorter oocyst survival (sr2=35%); vaccination still contributed (sr2=5%)
notes: supports vaccine utility but shows cat density and environmental persistence remain dominant control levers

design_summary: dose-response challenge model with free bradyzoites and intact cysts plus qPCR
key_finding: qPCR was more sensitive and several inocula established infection
partial schizonts and gamonts formed but no oocysts formed

design_summary: tracked homologous and heterologous rechallenge at 12, 24, 36 months
key_finding: protection waned over time and heterologous reinfection more readily re-induced shedding

cat_scale: 6 experimentally inoculated cats plus 1822 client-owned cats
design_summary: compared antibody kinetics after oral tissue-cyst versus sporulated-oocyst inoculation and modeled prevalence risk factors in Switzerland
key_finding: long-term humoral responses persisted; estimated true prevalence was 42.4% overall and 56.3% in outdoor cats vs 22.1% indoors; tissue-cyst and oocyst inoculations had similar early antibody kinetics
notes: useful for interpreting serology in vaccine and field surveillance work

cat_scale: mechanistic sequencing work with additional cat-shedding observations
design_summary: combined structural biology mutant sequencing and cat-passaging observations to dissect T-263 and TgO/GABA-AT
key_finding: TgO/GABA-AT knockout did not eliminate cat oocyst shedding; sequencing of T-263 linked blocked oocyst formation to conception and zygote-related candidate genes
notes: moves the field from phenomenological T-263 protection toward gene-defined transmission-blocking targets

cat_scale: systematic dataset of 47 studies with 256 positives among 9635 fecal samples
design_summary: generalized linear mixed models tested climate and anthropogenic predictors of shedding in free-ranging felids
key_finding: human population density was positively associated with shedding in domestic cats and wild felids; larger diurnal temperature range increased domestic-cat shedding
notes: helps frame where cat-targeted vaccination could have the largest environmental effect

cat_scale: comparative metagenomics of cats at sexual initiation oocyst excretion and uninfected stages
design_summary: shotgun metagenomics with KEGG CAZyme virulence-factor and taxonomic analyses
key_finding: sexual initiation and oocyst excretion reduced bacterial diversity; 39 KEGG pathways 106 CAZymes and 98 virulence factors differed; Bacteroides stercoris emerged as a candidate regulator
notes: mechanistic support for microbiota-informed interventions around oocyst excretion

cat_scale: feline detection study; exact sample size not extracted from current abstract snapshot
design_summary: evaluated MIC17A as a potential entero-epithelial and chronic-stage marker for feline toxoplasmosis
key_finding: MIC17A was proposed as a marker spanning entero-epithelial and chronic stages in cats
notes: useful for stage-specific feline detection and phase interpretation rather than direct vaccine efficacy

design_summary: developed a gra1-bag1 RT-qPCR workflow as an alternative to mouse bioassay for assessing Toxoplasma gondii viability
key_finding: combined RT-qPCR readouts offered a molecular route to assess viability without relying only on mouse bioassay
notes: useful for downstream evaluation systems and viability interpretation

cat_scale: cell-culture study in cyst-forming apicomplexans rather than cat model
design_summary: examined how BKI-1708 affected cytokinesis and stage conversion in Toxoplasma gondii and Neospora caninum
key_finding: BKI-1708 disrupted cytokinesis and promoted bradyzoite-related conversion, indicating that drug pressure can reshape parasite stage state
notes: important for drug-mechanism interpretation and stage-conversion context
